Every explicit transition endpoint (including the DoorShut self-loop on Cancel) is present with correct source and target. Every independently stated effect (stop timer on Cooking→DoorOpenWithItem; cancel/update cooking time on ReadytoCook→DoorShutWithItem) and every state action (display/update cooking time in ReadytoCook; start timer on Cooking entry) is captured. The guard "zero time set" on NL4's first alternative is correctly preserved in the transition group as a branch-selection condition, not duplicated as a standalone guard contract. No termination, progress, deadlock-freedom, state-retention, event-consumer-coverage, guard-disjointness, or cardinality obligations are established by the NL. No transition group is missing any alternative or shared-source relation.

decisions.reason: The NL explicitly uses conditional language ('if the door is closed with zero time set') which maps to guard semantics in state machine formalism. The transition group independently projects this as a guard field. The model has guard=null on transition:line:22 and guarded_transition_count=0 for the entire model. The S5 predicate was unsupported because 'zero time set' is a natural-language phrase not parseable by the FCSTM logical-expression grammar, but this is a W boundary (predicate/backend limitation), not a semantic resolution. The strongest rebuttal (business-level qualifier rather than formal UML guard) is self-defeating because the NL uses explicit 'if...with' conditionality and the transition group formally designates it as a guard. No competent alternative reading survives.

response.basis: Supplied numbered NL segments NL1–NL8, primary typed plan (21 contracts, 10 transition groups), and stage-context projection v8.
response.reason: I performed a segment-by-segment completeness check of all eight numbered NL segments against the 21 primary contracts and 10 transition groups. The NL describes a flat state machine with six states (DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking) and no composite hierarchy, so no containment, region, or initial-entry-under-owner obligations are established beyond the single system-level initial state already captured. Every explicit transition endpoint (including the DoorShut self-loop on Cancel) is present with correct source and target. Every independently stated effect (stop timer on Cooking→DoorOpenWithItem; cancel/update cooking time on ReadytoCook→DoorShutWithItem) and every state action (display/update cooking time in ReadytoCook; start timer on Cooking entry) is captured. The guard "zero time set" on NL4's first alternative is correctly preserved in the transition group as a branch-selection condition, not duplicated as a standalone guard contract.
